en: Using an inclined plane like a ramp reduces the lifting force needed to move heavy boxes, preventing back injuries.
Wearing rubber-soled shoes increases friction with the floor, preventing you from slipping and falling on wet surfaces.
Gravity accelerates falling objects downward, so wearing a helmet protects your head from severe impact injuries during bike crashes.
Never swallow small button magnets because they can attract each other inside your digestive tract and cause severe tissue damage.
Never touch electrical switches with wet hands because water conducts electricity and can cause a dangerous shock to your body.
Wearing sunglasses with UV protection blocks harmful ultraviolet light from damaging the sensitive retina cells inside your eyes.
Listening to loud music through headphones for extended periods permanently damages the tiny hair cells in your inner ear.
Wearing light-colored clothing on sunny days keeps your body cool because light colors reflect heat radiation instead of absorbing it.
Wearing a seatbelt safely absorbs your body's kinetic energy, preventing you from flying forward during a sudden car crash.
Using a wheelbarrow acts as a lever that multiplies your force, preventing muscle strain when moving heavy garden soil.
Rubbing your hands together rapidly converts mechanical energy into heat through friction, providing a quick way to warm cold fingers.
Carrying a heavy backpack tightly against your upper back lowers your center of gravity, preventing you from falling backward.
